subject: Recap: Reliability & graceful degradation discussion — Ledgerly
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Mila Orlov <mila@ledgerly.com>, Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-03T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Reliability & graceful degradation discussion — Ledgerly

Hi Mila / Arjun —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery focused on reliability and graceful degradation, plus suggested next steps so we keep momentum. Please flag anything I mis-stated.

Summary of pain points you shared
- Recent incidents: two production outages linked to a third-party feature store causing 20–30% request failures over ~45min (April and June).
- High tail latency when load spikes (95th percentile jumps >1.5s).
- Concern about model unavailability across regions during cloud maintenance windows.
- Need deterministic failover behavior (not opaque errors) to preserve UX.

Current stack
- Frontend: React + GraphQL
- Backend: Kubernetes (EKS us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 failover)
- Feature store: managed vendor (caching layer in front)
- Inference today: self-hosted FP16 LLMs on k8s (heterogeneous GPU fleet)

Success criteria you gave
- Recovery behavior: graceful fallback to a lower-cost/compatible model variant with documented degradation modes rather than errors.
- Target SLOs: 99.9% availability for inference endpoints; 95th latency < 500ms for short responses.
- Observable runbook: request-level tracing showing which model/region served the call, and easy policy to route to backup.
- Safe POC: demonstrable failover during a controlled outage (no data leaving Ledgerly tenancy).

Redwood suggestions discussed (high level)
- Multi-tier fallbacks: primary low-latency model in us-west, secondary quantized model in us-east, degraded responses served from prefix cache if both are unavailable.
- Automated routing policy: prefer latency SLOs but fail open to the next compatible model/region when capacity or health checks fail.
- Prefix/KV caching for common prompts to keep user-facing latency within target during transient spikes.
- Audit & tracing: token-level cost + latency breakdown and per-request traces to feed your observability stack.

Incident history notes we captured
- We can reproduce the failure mode you described in a controlled environment by throttling the feature store; graceful degradation requires both cached responses and model fallback policy.

Concrete next steps (recommended)
1) Vivek will share a one-page fallback architecture diagram & POC scope (attaching a draft).
2) Redwood to provide a redlineable SLA template and a proposed runbook that includes canary routing and automatic fallback policies (attached: redwood-sla-template.docx).
3) Schedule a 45-min SRE + infra working session week of Aug 11 to walk through a controlled failover test.
4) Ben will follow up with a ballpark commercial approach for a Dedicated/Reserved pool for your production critical flows.

Attachments: redwood-fallback-options.pdf (options matrix), redwood-sla-template.docx

If this looks good I’ll book the SRE session and share the HubSpot deal link for tracking.

Best,

Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

From: Arjun Patel <arjun.patel@ledgerly.com>

Cc: Mila Orlov <mila@ledgerly.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-03T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Reliability & graceful degradation discussion — Ledgerly

Thanks Camila — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications/questions from our side:

1) Regional failover: when you say "fallback to a model in us-east", what does the expected RTO look like (seconds/minutes)? We need to set realistic expectations for our product SLAs.
2) Cache-backed degraded responses: can we limit cache-only responses to a "read-only" UX so we avoid any risk of inconsistent writes?
3) Can you share example SLA language around outage credits vs. performance (latency) breaches?

Also adding context: our ops team is very sensitive to cross-region data egress and encryption-at-rest rules — we can allow cross-region compute but data must stay encrypted and audited.

Happy to join the SRE session week of Aug 11 — prefer Aug 12 or 13 afternoon PT.

-Arjun
Director, Platform Engineering | Ledgerly
arjun.patel@ledgerly.com | +1 510-555-0124

Date: 2025-08-04T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Draft arch + POC scope for Ledgerly (internal)

Looping you both in — I drafted the fallback architecture diagram and a concise POC scope (attached: ledgerly-poa-arch.drawio.png). Key points included in the doc:
- Primary: hosted low-latency variant in us-west-2 (quantized CPU/GPU hybrid); 99.95% target availability for this tier.
- Secondary: compatible quantized model in us-east-1 (cost-optimized, slightly higher median latency) used automatically when health checks or capacity thresholds are hit.
- Degraded mode: prefix/KV cache returns cached responses for the top ~5% of prompts; responses marked with a header indicating degraded confidence.
- Regional constraints: we will keep Ledgerly data encrypted in transit and at rest; cross-region compute limited to ephemeral inference cache only — no persistent feature materialization across regions.
- Observability: per-request metadata (model_id, region, fallback_reason) emitted to your tracing pipeline.

I also sketched the controlled failover test steps for the Aug 12 session. Attaching the file here.

Attachments: ledgerly-poa-arch.drawio.png (diagram)

Mila / Arjun — quick follow-up with the materials we promised and a proposed acceptance framework for the POC.

Attached: ledgerly-poa-arch.drawio.png, redwood-sla-template.docx (editable)

POC acceptance criteria (proposed)
- Functional: Redwood-backed inference handles 99% of baseline traffic under a 2x load spike without user-facing errors (measured during controlled test).
- Degradation behavior: During simulated feature-store outage, 95% of requests return either: a) fallback model response with documented quality delta, or b) cache response with a confidence header.
- Observability: each request surfaced in your tracing UI with model_id + region + fallback_reason tags.
- Security & compliance: no persisted Ledgerly PII leaves your VPC; cross-region compute limited to ephemeral containers with HSM-backed keys.

SLA examples (from template) — two options we discussed:
- Availability-first: 99.9% endpoint availability, credit schedule for full outages (similar to standard dedicated endpoint SLAs).
- Latency-first: 95th latency target 500ms; partial credits for sustained tail latency breaches.

On commercials: Ben will follow with a pricing note for a small Dedicated pool to meet the availability targets and a fall-through usage plan for bursts.

Next actions (I will take the lead)
- I’ll book the Aug 12 45-min SRE session (tentative: Aug 12 13:00 PT).
- Vivek to upload the diagram to the HubSpot deal and confirm the test checklist.
- Ben to provide a pricing ballpark by Aug 6.

If Aug 12 13:00 PT works, I’ll send a calendar invite and include our SRE/infra leads.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this into a safe POC.

Best,

Camila Reyes
